## Compare hospitals reporting both measures

Each point represents one hospital with available scores for both CMS measures during July 1, 2024–June 30, 2025. Hover over a point to see the hospital name, state, and both reported percentages.

The measures describe different imaging processes and use different clinical contexts. This chart is for exploring reported values—not for ranking hospitals or interpreting the relationship as a measure of quality.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

imaging_url <- "https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/sites/default/files/resources/d0134a9a89e59d49426cf5a2ad063b60_1792599881/Outpatient_Imaging_Efficiency-Hospital.csv"

hospital_scores <- read_csv(imaging_url, show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(
    Score = na_if(Score, "Not Available"),
    Score = as.numeric(Score)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(Score)) |>
  select(`Facility ID`, `Facility Name`, State, `Measure ID`, Score) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = `Measure ID`,
    values_from = Score
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(`OP-10`), !is.na(`OP-39`)) |>
  rename(
    ct_score = `OP-10`,
    recall_score = `OP-39`
  )
```

## OP-10 and OP-39 reported percentages

Use the hover details to inspect individual facilities. Hospitals missing either score are not shown; missing values are not treated as zero.

```{r}
plot_ly(
  data = hospital_scores,
  x = ~ct_score,
  y = ~recall_score,
  type = "scatter",
  mode = "markers",
  text = ~paste0(
    "Hospital: ", `Facility Name`,
    "<br>State: ", State,
    "<br>OP-10 abdomen CT: ", ct_score, "%",
    "<br>OP-39 screening recall: ", recall_score, "%"
  ),
  marker = list(
    color = "#167d8d",
    opacity = 0.55,
    size = 7
  ),
  hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>"
) |>
  layout(
    title = "Hospital-Reported Imaging Measures",
    xaxis = list(title = "OP-10 abdomen CT percentage (%)"),
    yaxis = list(title = "OP-39 screening recall percentage (%)")
  )
```

OP-10 tracks outpatient abdominal CT examinations performed both with and without contrast. OP-39 tracks screening mammograms followed by diagnostic imaging within 45 days. See the [CMS dataset](https://data.cms.gov/provider-data/dataset/wkfw-kthe) for the source records.
